bottom_line: Tech stocks just had their worst week since 2020, and the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is leaning toward raising rates again in December. That's a double hit: the AI excitement is cracking just as borrowing looks set to get more expensive.

stories.title: AI stocks get hammered
stories.real: AI and tech stocks got pummeled this week, the worst week for tech since 2020. Nvidia closed out its longest weekly losing streak since 2008, and one headline called it an 8% weekly crash.

stories.title: Fed likely raising rates again
stories.real: The Fed held rates steady after its first hike. Its meeting notes say higher rates are needed in December because inflation worries are growing, and markets put the odds of a December hike at over 90%.
stories.you: Loans, credit cards and mortgages could get more expensive, while savings accounts may pay a bit more.

stories.title: Shoppers holding up, for now
stories.real: US consumers are still spending despite inflation heading into the holidays. Slightly more people are filing for unemployment, though it's still low historically. Retail sales and inflation numbers come out next week, and some say there are bad signs ahead of the inflation report.
stories.you: Jobs are mostly holding, but prices are still squeezing budgets. Next week's numbers will show how much.
